paragraphs: Abba Shaul. Mishnah: Avot 2:8; Pe'ah 8:5; Kilayim 2:3; Shabbat 23:3; Eruvin folio 29; Beitzah 3:8; Shekalim 4:2; Ketubbot 7:6; Nedarim 6:5; Gittin 5:4; Kiddushin 4:2; Bava Metzia 4:12, 6:7; Bava Batra 2:7, 13; Sanhedrin 10:1; Makkot 2:2; Menahot 8:3, 11:5; Middot 2:5, 5:4. ‘Abba Shaul says; R' Akiva says’: Tosefta Kilayim chapter 3 [4:7 in the checked edition]. ‘Abba Shaul says,’ etc.; ‘R' Eleazar ben Yaakov says’: Tosefta Menahot 9:1. Ha-Mappelet 24b quotes Abba Shaul saying that he buried the dead. Once he chased a deer into a thighbone and ran for three parasangs without reaching its end. The checked Bavli gives R' Yohanan as an alternate attribution and says the identification of the bone as Og’s was told to the narrator afterward. In a second account, a cave opened beneath him and he stood in an eyeball up to his nose. He was afterward told that it was Avshalom’s eye. Lest you say Abba Shaul was a dwarf: he was tall in his generation. R' Tarfon reached his shoulder, R' Meir reached Tarfon’s, Rabbi reached Meir’s, R' Hiyya reached Rabbi’s, Rav reached Hiyya’s, and Rav Yehudah reached Rav’s. Bemidbar Rabbah adds R' Akiva between Tarfon and Meir. The Midrash’s sequence also omits R’ Hiyya. Adda the attendant (see his entry) reached Rav Yehudah’s shoulder. Pumbedita's Parshatkina—explained as a person's name—reached Adda the attendant's midpoint, while everyone else reached Parshatkina's waist. Tosafot write: the Arukh and Rashi explain it as a man's name, but this is not so, for then it should say ‘from Pumbedita.’ Rashbam explains it as an expression of provision and rule. End quotation. Rav Tzemah explains: a mighty man taller than all the people. Although they were indeed large in stature, Rashi, like the Arukh, cites this passage to explain Rav’s byname Abba Arikha, the truth is that wisdom diminished from generation to generation, for everything comes from teacher to pupil. Abba Shaul's wisdom was greater than all theirs; he ‘buried’ false arguments, which are dead (Yuhasin, chronological section). He and his wife are buried in Kefar Karya (גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]). [Glosses: Abba Shaul. Niddah 38a: Abba Shaul in Rav's name; needs examination. Not corrected [ל״ת, provisionally “not corrected”].]
